messages:
maya: Quick sync — we're finalizing the canary rollout config for model v2 -> v3 upgrades. Need agreement on percent ramps, step durations, abort/rollback guards, and a few edge cases (fractional traffic slices, concurrent rollouts). Thoughts?

ajay: my gut: 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100% with minimum hold times per step. keeps early blast radius tiny.

priya: agree on step sizes but we should make steps configurable per-route. paid customers can opt for faster ramps. also need a way to pin % to user segments (orgs/devs).

sam: two infra notes:
- KV-cache priming: when going from 0 -> 1% we still get cold cache for many keys. consider a prewarm phase where we route a small synthetic traffic to warm hot paths.
- capacity budget: simultaneous rollouts should not exceed a cluster-level percent (e.g., 15% of GPU pool) or we risk noisy neighbour SLOs.

zoe: console wants these UX primitives: expected qps per step, estimated time-to-next-step (based on hold time), a pause/resume button, and an emergency-cutoff (one-click rollback). also preview-to-internal flag for the first two steps.

ajay: putting a config sketch for API/CLI here:

```yaml
canary:
  steps: [1, 5, 20, 50, 100]
  hold_minutes: [15, 30, 60, 30, 0]  # last is finalization
  abort_conditions:
    - error_rate: {window: 5m, threshold_pct: 0.5}
    - latency_p95: {window: 5m, relative_increase_ms: 200}
  prewarm: true
  preview_internal_only: true
  capacity_budget_pct: 15
```

priya: couple of additions:
- quota-aware steps: if route has quota < X QPS, scale percentages to absolute requests so 1% isn't < 1 request/sec and useless.
- support fractional percentages like 0.1% for very high traffic routes (election traffic profiles).

sam: on abort semantics: do we auto-step-back or full-rollback? my recommendation: if transient spike (single window) step back to previous step and hold for longer, if sustained breach for 3 windows -> full rollback. also emit a takeover alert to oncall.

maya: telemetry needs: per-step telemetry buckets with: requests, failures, latency p50/p95/p99, client-id breakdown, and eval-checks (if customer has golden prompts). tie to alerting rules.

zoe: console note: show "expected user impact" calc: "at 5% you'll affect ~X requests/min (est)" and a small chart showing how many orgs/users in that bucket. helps PMs decide step sizes.

ajay: example CLI to create: `redwood rollout create --model v3 --canary @canary.yaml --name v3-rollout-2024-05` . backend should return rollout_id and per-step ETA.

deploy-bot: template saved: repo infra/rollouts/templates/canary_v1.yaml (PR 5123) :white_check_mark:

priya: one more policy: rate-limited ramping when backend telemetry shows high variance. i.e., if p95 noise > X, double hold time for next step automatically.

sam: also: guard against overlapping canaries on same model family. require an explicit override flag `--allow-concurrent` and enforce capacity_budget across all active rollouts.

maya: on quality regressions: we should define an eval harness metric threshold (e.g., delta in pass@k or semantic-similarity on prompt tests). if eval fails, immediate rollback, but only if eval set is representative.

ajay: implementation detail: store rollout state as CRD-like object: idempotent transitions, explicit current_step index, and a ledger of actions (who clicked next/pause/override). simplifies audit logs.

zoe: UX edge-case: what about fractional math when combining targeted segments? e.g., 1% internal + 2% prod = 3% total, but we should surface overlaps so people don't accidentally push > intended. console should show final aggregated percent per user cohort.

maya: actionable items:
- ajay: draft API + CRD schema + CLI (this week)
- zoe: console mockups for step view + aggregated percent warnings (by Fri)
- priya/sam: quota and capacity budget enforcement proposal (incl. fractional % handling)
- maya: define default abort rules for GA (error_rate 0.5%, latency_p95 +200ms, eval regressions)

ajay: one more nit: time units — prefer minutes for hold times and windows in config to avoid confusion.

priya: +1 on minutes. also we should support TTL for preview flags (auto-revoke after X days).

sam: emergency flow: console "cut traffic to 0% for this model across all routes" button that bypasses step logic and triggers rollback hooks. must require 2FA.

zoe: and an audit toast: who initiated the emergency and reason, captured in the rollout ledger.

maya: thanks all — i'll write the RFC with these points. if anyone has objections to defaults above, reply here. otherwise i'll open the PR and tag owners. :thumbsup:

ajay: LGTM. i'll kick off the API draft later today.

priya: OK from me.

sam: fine, just make sure oncall has a brief runbook for canary aborts.

zoe: noted, i'll add UX notes for emergency flow and warnings.

maya: closing loop — PR incoming.
